dossier.orientation: Buttondown is newsletter software where a solo publisher can add an unlimited number of collaborators under role-based permissions (draft-only or full sending access) for a flat add-on fee, and those collaborators do not add to the subscriber-based bill.

setup_conditions: Enabling collaborator roles requires purchasing the Teams add-on at +$79/month on top of base subscriber pricing (E16).

defining_need_fit.caveat: Unlimited collaborators (E14), the draft-only-vs-full-access role split (E15), and the exemption from per-subscriber billing (E13) are each directly documented and together cover the need's three literal components, but the audience's workflow also calls for withholding billing/API access from collaborators and for an ops person to handle subscriber questions and tagging specifically; the selected evidence does not state whether either role additionally restricts billing/API visibility or maps onto subscriber-tagging duties, so the complete workflow is only partially supported, and the Teams add-on carries its own $79/month setup cost.
defining_need_fit.why: E14 establishes unlimited collaborators, E15 establishes the exact draft-only-vs-full-access role split named in the need, and E13 establishes that collaborators don't affect the subscriber bill, together supporting the need's three stated components; the broader workflow's billing/API-access restriction and subscriber-tagging role scoping are not established by the selected evidence, so the complete task remains only partially supported.

ranked_relevance.why: Directly documents the exact draft-only-vs-full-access role split the audience's need names, letting an editor review copy without full account control.
Directly answers the 'without counting toward the per-subscriber bill' clause: team members are collaborators, not subscribers, and don't affect billing.
Documents the mechanism's lack of a headcount cap, supporting the premise that an editor and an ops person could both be added as the operation grows.
States the underlying billing mechanism (active subscribers only) that explains why non-subscriber collaborators do not add to cost, reinforcing E13's exemption claim.
Documents the necessary cost condition (+$79/month) for turning on collaborator roles at all, a material setup fact for a 1-3 person operation.
True CLI/API capability, but using it requires API credentials, which cuts against this audience's stated wish not to share billing/API access with a delegated collaborator.
Confirms API availability on all plans but says nothing about restricting a collaborator's API access, so it does not license a claim about scoped API exposure.
Generic qualitative praise about ease and fewer bugs, unrelated to collaborator permissioning or billing exemption specifics.
